facts.text: Stirling Castle, founded in 1129, is the city’s second oldest building and a key medieval stronghold.
The saying “he who holds Stirling holds Scotland” reflects Stirling’s historic role as the Gateway to the Highlands.
A ferry, later a bridge, across the River Forth at Stirling once brought wealth and strategic influence to the town.
The Wallace Monument, a towering tribute to the 13th‑century hero, stands beside Stirling Castle overlooking the city.
Every August, the Stirling Highland Games bring athletes, pipe bands, and craft stalls to the city’s historic grounds.
The old town’s medieval streets still echo with merchants’ trades, while the Old Bridge and port remain linked to Stirling’s rich past.
